minibus permisisti, multo magis iniquas eorum ca-
lumnias qui haud contenti me Bello isto lædi ma-
ximè, id Mundo persuadere conantur me id pri-
mo excitasse, vel primam Causam dedisse exci-
tandi.
Ea falsi-loquarum Linguarum confidentia est,
ut Mc propemodum in Innocentiæ Meæ sufficio-
nem adducant. Imo vel libens paterer (meo sa-
ltem silentio) tantum in Me reatum suscipere, mo-
do vel sic Hostium malitiam placare licuisset, po-
pulumque Meum ab hoc Bello Calamitoso redi-
mere, cum tu Domine cognoscas Innocentiam
Meam hac in Re.
Tu viros sanguinum, & Dolofos inveniessquo-
rum plurimi vix dimidiarunt dies suos, qui sibi
Ipsis improbarum Machinationum fructus olim,
& voluptatem spondebant.
Serva Domine famulum Tuum, quod adhuc fe-
cisti, & dissipa Gentes quæ Bella volunt.
Exurge Domine, & exaltare in commotionibus
hostium meorum, quæ jugiter crescunt, ascendunt
semper: Ecce qui conceperunt dolorem, parturie-
runt Injustitiam, & pepererunt mendacium.
Tu scis, id maximè in hoc Bello agi, ut vel
Personam Meam Interimant, vel vim faciant
Judicio, vel me cogant Conscientiæ Meæ, & Ve-
ritati renunciare.
In hoc sum, ut (optione, illi Davidis contra-
ria) optem potius illis Negando in Manus Homi-
num, crudeli utcunque Misericordia, quam in
Tuas Manus incidere peccando adversus Consci-
entiam

page.notes: Small printed mark after "tandi." and a small asterisk in the left margin beside "Exurge": ornaments or reference marks with no text, not transcribed. "Domine ƒ exaltare": the mark between the words is ambiguous and was read as a comma. "ut Mc" may be "Me" (uncertain reading, not marked in the text). The final word "entiam" is printed right-aligned after "Consci-" and is treated as the catchword. The right margin shows the edge of the neighbouring page (show-through), which is not transcribed.
